scope.objective: Reject lifecycle-semantic drift under reused versioned provider identities.

hypothesis.statement: Known V58 provider identities can accept execution-semantic mutations that change entry or exit behavior without a new strategy version.
hypothesis.root_cause: Several exact validators froze headline stop, target, and hold values but omitted provider position policy, fixed-versus-extended hold policy, recipe exit authority, profit-lock overlays, safety-stop overlays, or execution-side containment.

red_evidence.expected_failure: Each failure was DID NOT RAISE MultiAssetLiveConfigError.
accepted_drift_examples: BTC robust short entry delay 60 to 61 seconds
BTC robust short enter-and-close to flat-entry-only
BTC robust short fixed 24h hold to regime extension with 48h hard hold
BTC sweep recipe exit ignore to honor
SOL Hulk recipe exit ignore to honor
commodity fresh15 added completed-bar profit lock
BTC short-only signal provider relabeled with long execution authority

changes: Execution-side overrides must remain a subset of the provider's declared signal sides.
BTC robust/tuned short, BTC sweep, and ETH contracts now freeze timing, position policy, fixed hold, and neutral exit modifiers.
Reused SOL Hulk and commodity fresh15 contracts now reject unversioned recipe, lock, or safety-overlay drift.
HYPE alignment, SP500 fresh15, and SPCX cash-open contracts now reject safety-stop overlay drift.
V58 acceptance now asserts ETH/HYPE/SP500 effective sides and SP500's exact 100/40/80 completed-bar profit lock.

coverage_instrumentation.reason: The Python 3.13 coverage tracer failed during collection because numpy reported that its extension module could not be loaded more than once per process.
coverage_instrumentation.interpretation: No coverage percentage is claimed; normal fresh-process tests passed before and after this tooling failure.

uncertainties_and_failure_modes: This hardening covers known versioned V58 providers; an unknown future strategy identity still requires its own exact validator.
Passing config validation proves contract consistency, not source parity, profitability, liquidity, or execution quality.
The worktree contains extensive unrelated prior changes; this artifact binds exact current file bytes rather than claiming clean-branch provenance.
A future intentional exit or authority change must use a newly reviewed identity or explicitly update the frozen contract and tests.

confidence.basis: Every reported fail-open mutation was reproduced before the fix, rejected afterward, and all 59 discovered multi-asset profiles still load.

falsifiers: Any listed drift mutation validates successfully on the recorded source hashes.
Any published multi-asset profile fails solely because of this hardening.
Runtime binding bypasses validated provider execution contracts.
The recorded source hash or V58 profile hash does not match the referenced file.
